name: WA!DINING MANEKI 姫路城前店 (WA! Dining Maneki Himejijoumae)

claims.text: The kitchen prepares tempura (wheat-battered) alongside all other dishes. No dedicated fryer or allergen-separated preparation area is documented. Cross-contamination with wheat must be assumed.
The ekisoba broth contains powdered soy sauce as a listed ingredient. All savoury dishes served at this venue use the same broth base, meaning wheat via soy sauce is present throughout the menu.
Bonito and mackerel powder are core broth ingredients listed in the ekisoba product; there is no plant-based broth option. Every savoury dish contacts fish-based dashi.
No allergen-handling procedures or staff allergy training information is published on the official website or in any press materials reviewed.
Accepts credit cards and QR payments; non-smoking throughout; child-friendly; takeout available for packaged ekisoba and souvenir items.

name: 和ノ食 奏 (Wa no Shoku Kanade)

claims.text: The kitchen actively fries tempura — including the signature conger eel tempura with wheat batter — making shared-fryer cross-contamination a realistic concern. No dedicated GF fryer is mentioned.
Standard Japanese shoyu (wheat-containing) is the presumed base for sashimi service, nigiri, and cooked sauces. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is listed on the menu or website.
Fish dashi underpins virtually every dish in a traditional washoku kitchen of this type; no plant-based dashi option is disclosed.

No allergen menu, no published allergy protocol, and no review mentions of allergy accommodation were found across Tabelog, Hitosara, Gnavi, or the official website. Advance telephone inquiry is strongly recommended.
Some sashimi items are naturally free of added sauces and could in principle be ordered with rice only, keeping wheat exposure minimal if the kitchen is briefed in advance.

name: 洋食グリル天平 (Yoshoku Grill Tenpei)

claims.text: No dedicated GF fryer or preparation area is documented. The kitchen produces breaded tonkatsu (panko) and flour-thickened demi-glace simultaneously — cross-contamination is an inherent and unaddressed risk.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is expected in yoshoku cooking, including omelette rice and sauce bases. No tamari or wheat-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned on any source.
Meat stock, butter, egg, and dairy appear across the entire menu. No plant-based station or vegan workflow is documented.

No allergen menu, staff allergy training, or dietary accommodation protocol is mentioned on Tabelog, the official website, the tourism board listing, or any blog review. Diners with serious allergies should call ahead: 079-280-4697.
Chef Seki emphasises minimal use of chemical seasonings and additives, and sources pesticide-free local vegetables — a cleaner ingredient baseline than many casual yoshoku restaurants.

name: 夢乃蕎麦 大手前店 (Yumeno Soba Otemae-ten)

claims.text: The soba noodles are an 80/20 buckwheat-wheat blend — wheat is a core ingredient, not a trace contaminant. The kitchen handles wheat extensively (tempura, soba, soy sauce-based oden broth). No separate preparation area or dedicated fryer for wheat-free cooking has been reported.
Oden is served with ginger soy sauce (生姜醤油), which contains wheat. The standard soba tsuyu dipping broth also contains soy sauce. Wheat is present throughout the menu via soy sauce and soba noodles.

Virtually every dish contains fish-derived ingredients: soba broth is katsuobushi-based, oden items are predominantly fishcake (kamaboko, chikuwa, tsumire), and the restaurant is operated by a fish cake manufacturer. No vegan-safe preparation is identifiable.

name: 亜米麻辣湯 姫路店 (Yummy Mala Tang Himeji)

claims.text: All ingredients — including those that may contain wheat — are cooked in a shared beef-bone broth pot. No separation of wheat-containing and gluten-free noodles is confirmed.

The soup base ingredient list (beef bone broth, 20+ medicinal herbs and spices) is not fully disclosed. Condiments include sesame sauce and Sichuan peppercorn oil of unknown composition; soy sauce presence in the broth cannot be ruled out.
All ingredients are cooked in beef-bone broth; there is no plant-based broth option, so vegan cross-contact is certain.
No allergen sheet or staff allergy protocol is published on Tabelog, HotPepper, or the official website. Diners with allergies should call ahead (090-9615-5959) to discuss their needs.

Multiple wheat-free noodle options are available (sweet potato glass noodles, corn noodles, potato noodles, rice noodles) allowing diners to avoid wheat noodles specifically — though the broth wheat status remains unconfirmed.

name: 天邪鬼お好み焼き (Amanjaku Okonomiyaki)

claims.text: The teppan is used for wheat-batter okonomiyaki and wheat noodles, so any non-batter item cooked on the same surface would share heavy gluten cross-contact.
Standard okonomiyaki sauce and seasonings used at Hiroshima okonomiyaki shops are wheat-based; no wheat-free sauce is documented here.
Dishes are cooked on a shared teppan alongside pork, egg, and seafood, so cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.

name: 穴子と牡蠣 まめたぬき (Anago to Kaki Mametanuki)

claims.text: Fried oysters are a core menu item, implying a shared fryer; no dedicated gluten-free fryer is documented.
Anago rice and other dishes are seasoned with wheat-soy-sauce-based tare and standard Japanese soy sauce, which contain wheat.
All featured dishes are built around conger eel and oysters with fish-derived dashi/tare; no vegan or vegetarian preparation line is described.
Allergy information is noted as available, but no specific gluten-free or vegan handling protocol is published; guests would need to ask staff directly.

name: あなごめし 和田 (Anagomeshi Wada)

claims.text: The anago is finished with a sweet soy-based glaze (tare); standard Japanese soy sauce and such glazes contain wheat, making the dish unsuitable for a strict gluten-free diet.
The only dish served is grilled conger eel over rice with miso soup, so there are no vegan options and the kitchen is built entirely around fish.
